mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals a bottoming process in consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when the trigger is met in at least three out of five recession episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate margins, which in turn produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE > 4.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98 for three consecutive months signals a broad-based supply shock, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when INDPRO < 98 for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 200 for two consecutive months signals a deflationary shock, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when CPIAUCSL < 200 for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth > 0.4% monthly) and a fall in retail sales (RSAFS < previous 3-month average) signals a divergence between income and spending, suggesting precautionary savings and future demand weakness, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when the trigger is met in at least four out of ten episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for five consecutive months signals a robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month by > 200,000 for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of five consecutive months with PAYEMS growth > 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year decline in real GDP (GDPC1) below -1.5% for three consecutive quarters signals a deepening economic contraction, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -1.5% for 3 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of three consecutive quarters with GDPC1 YoY change < -1.5%.
